instruction: I want to prevent websites from tracking my location. How do I disable location access in Chrome?

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y
cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"session":{"restore_on_startup":4, "startup_urls":["http://funbrain.com/"]}}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.explanation: Task requires blocking location access for all websites in Chrome. Similar complexity - navigate to Settings > Privacy and security > Site settings > Location and block access.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads Chrome's geolocation preference from the Preferences file (profile.default_content_setting_values.geolocation)
Correctly interprets geolocation=2 as 'blocked' and returns 'true' as expected
Metric (exact_match) appropriately compares result against expected value 'true'
Complete coverage: instruction requires blocking location access, evaluator checks exactly that requirement
Cross-platform support: handles Windows, macOS, and Linux file paths correctly
Getter reads from persisted file system state, not transient UI state, so no postconfig needed despite heuristic warning
Expected value 'true' is semantically correct for verifying location blocking
